title: "Resources"

This module introduces no new regulation, standard, or framework, and no new source was fetched
for it. It crosswalks ITIL (Information Technology Infrastructure Library) vocabulary — described
in this curriculum's own words, never cited to a specific AXELOS/PeopleCert publication — onto two
already-built vocabularies: NIST's (National Institute of Standards and Technology) Risk Management
Framework, already applied to the eQMS (electronic quality-management system) in
`grc-frameworks-and-risk-management`, and ISO/IEC 27001's own Annex A control-domain structure,
already opened for a vendor's certificate in `vendor-and-third-party-risk-management`. The first five links
below are the direct inputs this module reasons against, by name, without redeveloping any of
them; the last five are external sources (including this lesson's video) for going deeper.

- **[Risk Management Frameworks Side by
  Side](../../grc-frameworks-and-risk-management/risk-frameworks-side-by-side/index.qmd)** — the
  module that first laid RMF, ISO 31000, and ICH Q9 (International Council for Harmonisation
  Quality Risk Management guideline) side by side and quoted the Categorize and Monitor purpose
  statements in full. Read it for the complete, unabridged text this module restates only one short
  fragment of, and for the honest caveat — repeated again here — that RMF is a voluntary structure
  Lakeshore borrowed, not a federal requirement.

- **[Categorize and Select
  Controls](../../grc-frameworks-and-risk-management/categorize-and-select-controls/index.qmd)** —
  the module this lesson's first crosswalk draws its facts from directly: the eQMS's own reasoned
  moderate-impact categorization and the three control families (account and identity management,
  audit/logging, physical and environmental protection) selected and tailored to it. Read it for
  the full reasoning this module references but doesn't re-derive.

- **[Authorize and
  Monitor](../../grc-frameworks-and-risk-management/authorize-and-monitor/index.qmd)** — the
  module this lesson's second crosswalk is built entirely from: the Director's authorization
  decision accepting the quarterly access-review gap as a named, 30-day residual risk, and the
  full five-part ongoing monitoring plan this module re-expressed as a continual improvement
  register. Read it for the actual decision, word for word, including why authorizing with one
  open item was the defensible call.

- **[Reading an ISO 27001
  Certificate](../../vendor-and-third-party-risk-management/reading-an-iso-27001-certificate/index.qmd)**
  — the module this lesson's third crosswalk reuses its six general ISO 27001 Annex A domain
  names from (access control, supplier relationships, change management, incident management,
  business continuity, asset management), paraphrase-only, no control number invented in either
  module. Read it for the fuller explanation of what an ISMS (Information Security Management
  System) certification actually certifies, the Stage 1/Stage 2 audit structure, and why a
  certificate's stated scope is the first thing any reader should check — all background this
  module's own "what if" conversation assumes without re-teaching.

- **[ITIL-to-QSE Crosswalk: CMDB and Continual
  Improvement](../itil-to-qse-crosswalk-cmdb-and-continual-improvement/index.qmd)** — this course's
  own module 2, for the exact eQMS CMDB entry (including its honest blank qualification-status row)
  this module's first crosswalk builds directly on, and for the same honest-mapping method ("close
  enough to be worth mapping, different enough to name the gap") this module continues rather than
  reinvents.

- **[ICOR Webinar: ITIL 4 and Risk Management. September, 27 2023](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WFsbK1vM_r8)**
  (ICOR Education, from oEmbed `author_name`) — the video embedded in this lesson. An ITIL
  training provider's webinar on risk management in ITIL 4: the ITIL-side vocabulary this module
  bridges from. General ITSM training, not blood-specific and not about RMF or ISO 27001; only its
  title was checked, so watch it as background. Verified embeddable via YouTube oEmbed on
  2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[NIST: About the Risk Management Framework](https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/risk-management/about-rmf)**
  — NIST's own overview of the seven-step RMF whose Categorize, Select, and Monitor steps this
  module crosswalks to. Read it for the authoritative, current description of the steps.
  Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[NIST Cybersecurity Framework](https://www.nist.gov/cyberframework)** — NIST's CSF home page.
  A lighter, outcome-based companion to RMF that organizations often use alongside ISO 27001;
  useful if your CIO frames security in CSF terms rather than RMF steps. Verified loading via
  `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[NIST Online Informative References (OLIR) Program](https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/olir)** —
  NIST's catalog of published mappings between frameworks and standards. Read it to see how
  formal crosswalks are built and reviewed, which is the discipline behind this lesson's honest
  "clean match, partial fit, no counterpart" reasoning. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11
  (HTTP 200).

- **[PeopleCert: ITIL 4 Practitioner: Information Security Management](https://www.peoplecert.org/browse-certifications/it-governance-and-service-management/ITIL-1/itil-4-practitioner-information-security-management-3873)**
  — the ITIL certification body's own page for the security management practice this module
  crosswalks. It describes the practice's scope, not its copyrighted text; this curriculum still
  describes ITIL in its own words. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

## Keep learning

Not official sources — good places to learn more about governance, risk and control frameworks that sit beside ITIL.

- **[CISSP Certified Information Systems Security Professional](https://www.isc2.org/certifications/cissp)** (ISC2) — the official exam outline page. Domain 1 (Security and Risk Management) is the closest match to this crosswalk's governance and risk themes. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[COBIT | Control Objectives for Information Technologies](https://www.isaca.org/resources/cobit)** (ISACA) — overview of the IT governance framework often mapped alongside ITIL; shows how governance and management objectives are separated. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[CRISC Certification](https://www.isaca.org/credentialing/crisc)** (ISACA) — the risk-and-controls certification page; its domains show how IT risk practitioners organize the same ground. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[ISACA Journal](https://www.isaca.org/resources/isaca-journal)** (ISACA) — peer-written practitioner articles on IT governance, risk and service management; browse for ITIL-and-governance pieces. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
